arxiv-2007-14743.title: Prediction of the in situ coronal mass ejection rate for solar cycle 25: Implications for Parker Solar Probe in situ observations Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2007-14743.creator: Christian Möstl, Andreas J. Weiss, Rachel L. Bailey, Martin A. Reiss, Tanja Amerstorfer, Jürgen Hinterreiter, Maike Bauer, Scott W. McIntosh, Noé Lugaz, David Stansby
arxiv-2007-14743.description: Abstract The Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter missions are designed to make groundbreaking observations of the Sun and interplanetary space within this decade. We show that a particularly interesting in situ observation of an interplanetary coronal mass ejection (ICME) by PSP may arise during close solar flybys ( < 0.1 <0.1 AU).

arxiv-2107-06428.title: For high-dimensional hierarchical models, consider exchangeability of effects across covariates instead of across datasets
arxiv-2107-06428.creator: Brian L. Trippe, Hilary K. Finucane, Tamara Broderick
arxiv-2107-06428.description: Abstract Hierarchical Bayesian methods enable information sharing across multiple related regression problems. While standard practice is to model regression parameters (effects) as (1) exchangeable across datasets and (2) correlated to differing degrees across covariates, we show that this approach exhibits poor statistical performance when the number of covariates exceeds the number of datasets.

arxiv-2210-16750.title: Mass-Metallicity Relation during the Epoch of Reionization in the CROC Simulations Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2210-16750.creator: Isaac Noel, Hanjue Zhu (朱涵珏), Nickolay Y. Gnedin
arxiv-2210-16750.description: Abstract The low-redshift mass-metallicity relation (MZR) is well studied, but the high-redshift MZR remains difficult to observe. To study the early MZR further, we analyze the Cosmic Reionization on Computers (CROC) simulations with a focus on the MZR from redshifts 5 to 10.

arxiv-2307-03634.title: Applications of the Klein-Gordon equation in the Feshbach-Villars representation in the non-inertial cosmic string space-time
arxiv-2307-03634.creator: Abdelmalek Bouzenada, Abdelmalek Boumali, Edilberto O. Silva
arxiv-2307-03634.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Abdelmalek Bouzenada, Abdelmalek Boumali, Edilberto O. Silva. We study the relativistic quantum motion of a spineless particle using the Feshbach-Villars (FV) formalism in the spinning cosmic string spacetime. The movement equations are derived using the first-order FV formulation of the Klein-Gordon (KG) equation. We apply the equation of motion (a) to study the motion of the particle confined to a rigid-wall potential, (b) motion in the presence of a Coulomb-type potential, and (c) particle interacting with the Feshbach-Villars oscillator (FVO).

arxiv-2312-03593.title: Streaming Algorithms for the k k -Submodular Cover Problem
arxiv-2312-03593.creator: Wenqi Wang, Gregory Gutin, Yaping Mao, Donglei Du, Xiaoyan Zhang
arxiv-2312-03593.description: Abstract Given a natural number k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 , we consider the k k -submodular cover problem ( k k -SC). The objective is to find a minimum cost subset of a ground set 𝒳 \mathcal{X} subject to the value of a k k -submodular utility function being at least a certain predetermined value τ \tau .

arxiv-2411-13707.title: High-degree cubature on Wiener space through unshuffle expansions
arxiv-2411-13707.creator: Emilio Ferrucci, Timothy Herschell, Christian Litterer, Terry Lyons
arxiv-2411-13707.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Emilio Ferrucci, Timothy Herschell, Christian Litterer, Terry Lyons. Utilising classical results on the structure of Hopf algebras, we develop a novel approach for the construction of cubature formulae on Wiener space based on unshuffle expansions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by constructing the first degree-7 cubature formula on d d -dimensional Wiener space with drift in the sense of Lyons and Victoir [ 25 ] which is explicit as a function of an underlying Gaussian cubature.

arxiv-2411-18728.title: The Last Mile to Supervised Performance: Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2411-18728.creator: Daniel Morales-Brotons danimoralesbrotons@gmail.com, Grigorios Chrysos chrysos@wisc.edu, Stratis Tzoumas stratis.tzoumas@zeiss.com, Volkan Cevher volkan.cevher@epfl.ch
arxiv-2411-18728.description: Abstract Supervised deep learning requires massive labeled datasets, but obtaining annotations is not always easy or possible, especially for dense tasks like semantic segmentation. To overcome this issue, numerous works explore Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA), which uses a labeled dataset from another domain (source), or Semi-Supervised Learning (SSL), which trains on a partially labeled set.

arxiv-2504-05866.title: CTI-HAL: A Human-Annotated Dataset for Cyber Threat Intelligence Analysis
arxiv-2504-05866.creator: Sofia Della Penna, Roberto Natella, Vittorio Orbinato, Lorenzo Parracino, Luciano Pianese
arxiv-2504-05866.description: Abstract Organizations are increasingly targeted by Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs), which involve complex, multi-stage tactics and diverse techniques. Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) sources, such as incident reports and security blogs, provide valuable insights, but are often unstructured and in natural language, making it difficult to automatically extract information.

arxiv-2504-15126.title: The topology of the configuration spaces and the independence complexes for digraphs
arxiv-2504-15126.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . We study the topology of the (path) configuration spaces and the (path) independence complexes for digraphs as well as their underlying graphs. We prove some canonical embeddings from the (path) independence complexes of the underlying graphs to the (path) independence complexes of the digraphs as well as some canonical embeddings between the (path) independence complexes induced by strong totally geodesic immersions of (di)graphs. We apply the path complexes and the path homology to the path independence complexes of (di)graphs.

arxiv-2509-09430.title: Supersymmetric truncation of 𝒩 = 3 \mathcal{N}=3 dilaton Weyl multiplet
arxiv-2509-09430.creator: Soumya Adhikari, Aravind Aikot, Eswar Krishnan and, Bindusar Sahoo
arxiv-2509-09430.description: Abstract We perform a supersymmetric truncation of the 𝒩 = 3 \mathcal{N}=3 dilaton Weyl multiplet with an R-symmetry S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) SU(2)\times U(1)\times U(1) , to obtain a 32 + 32 32+32 off-shell representation of 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 conformal supergravity.

arxiv-2509-10601.title: Active galactic nuclei do not exhibit stably periodic brightness variations
arxiv-2509-10601.creator: Kareem El-Badry 1,2, David W. Hogg 2,3,4, Hans-Walter Rix 2
arxiv-2509-10601.description: Abstract Periodic variability in active galactic nuclei (AGN) light curves has been proposed as a signature of close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries. Recently, 181 candidate SMBH binaries were identified in Gaia DR3 based on periodicity in their ∼ \sim 1000-day light curves.

arxiv-2601-17104.title: Euler-Poincaré Formulation of Barotropic Fluids Coupled with ADM Gravity
arxiv-2601-17104.creator: Allan Louie
arxiv-2601-17104.description: Abstract This paper develops a geometric mechanics framework for the reduction of general relativistic hydrodynamic variational principles, from the variation of worldlines approach in 4D spacetime to 3-dimensional Eulerian descriptions. We consider a self-gravitating, barotropic fluid and obtain the Euler-Poincaré equations of the system by Lagrangian reduction.

arxiv-2602-23531.title: Extending Ground-Based Gravitational-Wave Sensitivity to 5 Hz
arxiv-2602-23531.creator: Amit Singh Ubhi, Lari Koponen, Jiri Smetana, Yulin Xia, Haixing Miao, Emilia Chick, John Bryant, Geraint Pratten, Teng Zhang, Richard Mittleman, Peter Fritschel, Alan V. Cumming, Giles Hammond, Denis Martynov
arxiv-2602-23531.description: Abstract Extending the sensitivity of terrestrial gravitational-wave detectors below 20 Hz is a long-standing challenge, limited by ground motion and inertial sensing noise. In this letter, we demonstrate ultra-high-vacuum compatible inertial isolation and position sensing technologies that achieve active platform stabilization down to 10 mHz.

pmc-11510157.title: Is Fasting Superior to Continuous Caloric Restriction for Weight Loss and Metabolic Outcomes in Obese Adults? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
pmc-11510157.creator: Víctor Siles-Guerrero, Jose M. Romero-Márquez, Rosa Natalia García-Pérez, Cristina Novo-Rodríguez, Juan Manuel Guardia-Baena, María Hayón-Ponce, Carmen Tenorio-Jiménez, Martín López-de-la-Torre-Casares, Araceli Muñoz-Garach
pmc-11510157.description: Background: fasting-based strategies (FBS) and continuous caloric restriction (CCR) are popular methods for weight loss and improving metabolic health. FBS alternates between eating and fasting periods, while CCR reduces daily calorie intake consistently. Both aim to create a calorie deficit, but it is still uncertain as to which is more effective for short- and long-term weight and metabolic outcomes.

pmc-12657626.title: Applying Critical Thinking Frameworks in Public Health: A Systematic Review of Strategic Approaches to Enhance Decision‐Making and Policy Development

pmc-12657626.description: Background and AimsCritical thinking play a vital role in enhancing public health decision‐making by enabling professionals to assess interventions, address complex challenges, and formulate effective policies. Despite the intensive and continuous use of synthetic fungicides, diseases severity has not reduced and control has become increasingly challenging; therefore, the search for environmentally friendly and sustainable products has intensified.

pmc-12974664.title: Biofilm Associated Persistence and Drug Tolerance in Mycobacteria Within Host Microenvironments
pmc-12974664.creator: Lourdes Serrano Garcia, Cesar Augusto Roque‐Borda, Fernando Rogério Pavan, Marlus Chorilli
pmc-12974664.description: Biofilms formed by mycobacteria, particularly Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), represent a major challenge in tuberculosis (TB) treatment due to their highly organized structure and their capacity to induce phenotypic drug tolerance. These three‐dimensional bacterial aggregates are embedded in a self‐produced extracellular matrix that restricts antibiotic penetration and shields bacilli from host immune responses.

pmc-13584015.title: Which types of research and knowledge translation are most likely to lead to public health-informed policy responses to unhealthy commodities? A UK-based cross-sectional survey and focus group-based study
pmc-13584015.creator: Alice Fabbri, Britta Katharina Matthes, Katherine E Smith
pmc-13584015.description: IntroductionProducts of unhealthy commodity industries (UCIs) are major drivers of non-communicable diseases. The role of evidence in supporting regulation of these products remains underexplored. This study examined how different types of research and knowledge translation activities influenced policy change across unhealthy commodities.MethodsA study was conducted combining an online survey and three focus groups.

pmc-13616439.title: Polyphenolic and Biogenic Volatile Organic Compound Profiles of Endemic Metallophytes From the Thallium‐Rich Allchar Mining Area

pmc-13616439.description: The Allchar Mining Area (North Macedonia) is an extreme metalliferous environment enriched in Tl, As and Sb that supports diverse endemic metallophytes. This study investigates metabolic profiles in selected species through integrated analysis of polyphenols (HPLC/DAD/MSn) and biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs, headspace GC–MS). A total of 78 polyphenols and 123 volatile compounds were identified.
